title: The `volatile` keyword: what it guarantees and what it does not

videos.script: Lesson 12 ended with a worker that never saw a flag. One word fixes it. {{fix}} Mark the field volatile, run the same program, and the worker stops a moment after main sets the flag. {{order}} volatile does two things. Every read sees the latest write. And everything written before a volatile write is visible to whoever reads it afterwards, which makes it a way to hand over a whole batch of data. {{not}} What it does not do is make two steps into one. Four threads each add one to a volatile counter a million times, and the total comes out short by more than half. {{when}} So volatile is the right tool for a flag, a status, or a reference to an immutable object, and the wrong one for anything that reads, changes and writes.
